facts.fact: The IMPULSE study (Nov 2022-Jul 2024) found DHIS2 in use as the routine health information system in central and subnational data offices in Ethiopia.

A cross-sectional survey of 220 staff in public health facilities in Harari Regional State and Dire Dawa City Administration (June-July 2020) found DHIS2 in use there, with about 45% of staff using its data.

note: Describes the community-level eCHIS for Health Extension Program services, not the national routine facility reporting system; no statement on the national HMIS.
The document concerns the education system only and states nothing on health reporting.

facts.fact: Gates Foundation's 2023 grant record says the funds are to help the Ministry of Health upgrade and maintain the national HMIS and build digital tools for data use (USD 4,798,310, 2023-2027).
Gates Foundation's IATI record funds HABTech Solutions from 2023-11-08 to capacitate Ethiopia's health ministry to upgrade and maintain the national HMIS.
The DHIS2 profile says that as of 2024 DHIS2 data collection covered all of Ethiopia's 30,000+ public health facilities, giving routine data on health services and outcomes.
The profile says weekly notifiable disease surveillance data has been integrated into the DHIS2-based Public Health Emergency Management (PHEM) system.
The Ethiopian Journal of Health Development case study says the Ministry of Health has used an HMIS since 2008 and moved to a unified DHIS2 in 2017 to integrate data across all regions and programs.
